Planetary Parasitism

Gog (DC Comics) is an Old God from the Third World who rooted himself to the Earth with the consequence that if he left, the earth would die shortly after.

Power/Ability to:

Be a planetary parasite.

The ability to root oneself into any planet and completely drains its life-force. Sub-power of Cosmic Hunger. Variation of Parasite Physiology and Planetary Empowerment. Not to be confused with Planetary Merging and Planetary Energy Absorption.

Also Called[]

  • Planet/Terrain/World Consumption/Devouring/Draining/Eating/Leeching/Parasitism/Vampirism
  • Planetary Consumption/Devouring/Draining/Eating/Leeching/Vampirism

Capabilities[]

The user can drain the bio-kinetic energies held within entire planets and leave them to wither into barren wastelands upon departure. This ability makes it especially difficult for an opponent to destroy the user, as the user essentially integrates their existence into the survival of the world they are currently placed on.

Alternatively, the user can outright consume planets to satisfy their hunger.

Limitations[]

  • User's body must be stable enough to contain the bio-kinetic energies that are absorbed, or the user will become unstable and may be destroyed
  • If only the control center of the user's body is disconnected, while the integrated segment of the user's body is left unharmed, the user's power is nullified.

Gallery[]

Lavos (Chrono Trigger) burrows into the core of a planet to feed and rest, and upon reaching full maturity, it bursts forth from the core, destroying the planet.
Pyron (Darkstalkers) consumes entire worlds, assimilating them into his personal galaxy.
Mother Mercy (DC Comics) is a planetary psionic parasite capable of controlling its spawn, the Black Mercy, as well as its own biospheric ecosystem.
Moro (Dragon Ball Super) lives up to his epithet of "Planet-Eater."
Jenova (Final Fantasy VII series) lands on a host planet and subverts it in order to reproduce and spread.
King Ghidorah (Godzilla: Planet Eater) uses gravitational power to eat planets.
The Tree of Might (Dragon Ball Z: The Tree of Might) drains life force from a planet in order to grow its fruit.
Leviathans (Metroid Prime) are living meteors that infest planets turning them into copies of Phaaze.
Metarexes (Sonic X) drain Planet Eggs to utilize their power, condemning the host planets to a slow death.
Ego (Marvel Cinematic Universe) planted extensions on other planets as part of his “expansion.”
